data.narrative:
Biofire, a Series A defense and security company founded by Kai Kloepfer, has raised $52.9M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 10 same-sector peers at Series A/B stage, comprising 8 private companies (including Anduril Industries, Helsing, and Shield AI) and 2 public benchmarks (DRSHF, IDEAFORGE.NS). The peer set spans $125M to $3.0B in valuation.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis uses the $52.9M raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A advancement, yielding $106M. Peer-median analysis across the 10-company comp set produces a $1.0B implied valuation, with a range of $125M (floor) to $3.0B (ceiling). The peer median is anchored by Series B-stage companies including Dream Security ($3.0B), Harmattan AI ($1.4B), and Code Metal ($1.2B).

The triangulated analysis supports a valuation range of $90M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $553M. This wide spread reflects material uncertainty around market maturation, customer concentration, and the stage-gap between Biofire's Series A position and the predominantly Series B composition of the peer set. The peer-median method's $1.0B result likely reflects upward bias from later-stage comps; the stage-progression floor of $106M may understate defensible value given sector dynamics.
